newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end flat as early gains slashed.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end flat as early gains slashed.

text.p: The Australian share market ended a choppy day's trade little changed on Monday with a falling afternoon futures market wiping out early record-breaking gains.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed 1.2 points lower at 2,524.8 having touched a record high of 2,538 mid-morning, surpassing Friday's previous record high of 2,528.1.
The strong start failed to last as nerves ahead of Tuesday's Federal budget seemed to get the better of traders, although activity was moderate rather than heavy.
"The futures lost their nerve in the afternoon," said a Sydney-based broker, noting that most had not expected much movement ahead of the government's second budget.
"Volumes are okay but nothing sensational. We called it with only five or so points in it at best and that is the way it has ended up."

Definitive reasons for the afternoon's losses proved elusive with brokers saying they could only put it down to investors taking a defensive stance ahead of Tuesday night's release of the 1997/98 fiscal programme.

Among individual stocks building materials, sugar and aluminium group CSR was the feature, posting a sharply lower full year net profit of A$212 million, citing a continued subdued housing industry for the softer result. Its shares ended just A$0.007 lower at A$4.763 (US$3.72) with brokers suggesting the result had failed to surprise.

Gold miners Acacia Resources, up nine cents to A$2.04, Plutonic Resources, up 15 cents to A$5.10, and Sons of Gwalia, up 17 at A$5.63, were the pick of the precious metals miners boosted by the stronger gold price.
